did_you_know.text: Did you know? The man of God who came to Bethel was sent by the LORD from Judah, while Jeroboam was standing beside the altar and offering incense.
Did you know? The prophecy concerning the altar at Bethel mentioned Josiah by name—a descendant of David who would one day burn the priests of the high places and human bones on it.
Did you know? The sign accompanying the prophecy was that the altar would split apart and its ashes would spill out. This happened when Jeroboam heard the prophecy.
Did you know? When Jeroboam stretched out his hand to seize the man of God, his hand withered, and he could not pull it back.
Did you know? After Jeroboam asked for prayer, the man of God prayed to the LORD, and the king’s hand was restored as it had been before.
Did you know? The man of God received a special command not to eat bread or drink water in Bethel, and not to return by the way he had come.

Did you know? The old prophet from Bethel claimed that an angel had spoken to him in the LORD’s name and commanded him to bring the man of God back to his house, but the text explicitly says, “He lied to him.”

Did you know? After the man of God was killed by a lion, the lion did not eat the body or attack the donkey standing beside it—a remarkable sight that underscored the significance of what had happened.
Did you know? The old prophet buried the man of God in his own tomb and mourned him with the words, “Alas, my brother,” even though he himself had misled him earlier.

Did you know? Despite the prophecy, the sign, and the miracle, Jeroboam did not turn from his evil ways. He continued appointing priests for the high places from among anyone who wanted the position; this act was considered the sin of the house of Jeroboam.
